subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Court of Fontaine

140151001.text: Stocking up on materials, confirming construction timelines, discussing compensation terms with families affected by the disaster... Between all of that, I've been making a lot of trips between the Court and Poisson.

140151004.text: Well, though the victims have received relief payments from the Court, in my opinion, as the administrators of Poisson, Spina di Rosula should take some responsibility as well.

140151005.text: Our financial situation right now isn't the best, so all we've been doing is signing agreements for the damages to be repaid at a later date.

140151006.text: Though just pieces of paper now, they demonstrate our commitment. They're necessary to restore the people's faith in us.

140151007.text: Whoa, spoken like a true President... You are a really responsible leader! That must be taking up most of your time though, right?

140151008.text: Oh, you bet. Between that and all the other errands I have to run at the Court, I'm always forgetting one thing or another.

140151009.text: So before I came over this time, I took a page from Melus' book and decided to make a list of everything. This way, it's easy to see which tasks you haven't checked off.

140151011.text: And then... Since Melus loved using shorthand, I decided to also follow his example, and come up with some shorthand of my own.

140151012.text: But after running a few errands in the city, I'm kind of struggling to even read my own handwriting anymore, hehe...

140151013.text: That does sound like you all right... So what kind of shorthand did you use?

140151015.text: Let Paimon see... Wait, there's nothing here but a bunch of weird symbols!

140151016.text: This looks like... a piece of kelp wrapped around a stick? And this other one... Um, is it supposed to be a boar in a box?

140151017.text: Hmm... The first one has to do with confirming the final payment amount for the fishermen, while the second one is a reminder to try the new burger that just hit the market!

140151018.text: Okay, Paimon can definitely see how you might forget what each of these means!

140150201.text: The engineer is still doing a few routine safety checks. We can head out as soon as we get the green light!

140150202.text: So, Paimon has always wanted to ask... The three aquabus lines are all named after people in your family, right?

140150203.text: Yeah, that's right. Callas and Navia are self-explanatory, while Clementine was the name that my mother went by.

140150204.text: Spina di Rosula was one of the main sponsors for the construction, right?

140150205.text: If you provided the Mora to build the lines, then why isn't there even a dedicated line to Poisson?

140150206.text: Spina di Rosula built all the lines, yet you still have to take a special boat just to go home... Paimon doesn't get it.

140150207.text: Well, what I heard is that most of our businesses don't actually use Poisson as a hub, so there was no real reason to build a line straight to Poisson.

140150208.text: You are right that it is a bit strange, though. If you've already committed to build three lines, why not just add a fourth?

140150209.text: Yeah, that's what Paimon's saying! The aquabus is so convenient, it's really a huge shame.

140150210.text: Well, it is what it is. You know what my father was like — even I often struggled to figure out what was going on in his head.

140150213.text: Hehe, but that would only be the case if he cared about what others thought. My father was always really stubborn. Once he made up his mind, good luck getting him to change it.

140150214.text: From what I've heard, the rights of all the other members of the Spina only went as far as giving him advice or suggestions, and no further. That included my mother, too.

140150215.text: Huh... Well, that explains why you weren't on the greatest of terms with him.

140150216.text: Yeah, because I wouldn't just let him keep getting his way! He was just... *sigh* not very agreeable.

140150217.text: Boss, the boat's ready! We can head out.

140150301.text: It'll be a while before we get to Poisson. Let's keep talking.

140150302.text: Hmm, Navia, what was your mother like as a person?

140150303.text: Oh, Paimon's sorry, she totally forgot that you mentioned before that she passed away during childbirth, so you probably don't remember her at all...

140150304.text: Hahaha, that's alright! I've heard many stories about her from the rest of the Spina. They've always said that they were sure we would have gotten along famously.

140150305.text: While my papa was stiff like a board, my mother was supposedly super cheerful and funny. Their complementary personalities allowed them to make up for each other's flaws.

140150306.text: My father would run the businesses and expand our reach, while my mother would keep the peace and make sure that everyone was happy. Their work made sure that the Spina could grow and thrive.

140150307.text: Sounds like they were not just a well-matched couple, but fantastic business partners as well!

140150308.text: Yeah, but those are just stories and anecdotes after all. It's hard for me to piece together a more complete or intimate picture of her.

140150309.text: But sometimes, I'd still look at the Clementine Line and wonder... Would the Spina and Poisson still be what they are today, had my mother survived?

140150310.text: Silver once said that a name is a kind of inscription — a way to etch a memory into the world. When given a name, a cold, inanimate object can gain a completely new meaning.

140150311.text: So, I will always associate the Line with her in my heart.

140150312.text: Over the past few weeks, I've also begun to appreciate how water can take in and hold our most intense feelings and memories, as well as how one may reflect on their past by watching the sea.

140150313.text: I've lost many beloved people and memories to the sea. Even though I cannot stop for them, and must continue to keep moving...

140150314.text: The fact won't change that they existed in my life, and gave me the reason and motivation to move forward.

140150316.text: Always, but no matter what, we can't change the past.

140150319.text: But I tell myself that I need to keep looking towards the future. Everyone, even my parents, have all already overcome so many obstacles.

140150320.text: Besides, I'm the President of Spina di Rosula. I've got to keep my chin up.

140150318.text: Of course. I still haven't really gotten used to a life without them...

140150321.text: We've reached the shore. Let's go — I'll show you the new Poisson.

140150322.text: Navia... Do you think she's doing alright?

140150325.text: Okay, Paimon supposes you're right... She's really been through a lot. It couldn't have been easy, shouldering so much by herself...

140151102.text: Huh!? But aren't you supposed to...

140151103.text: Oh, well if it isn't Colter! Back already from the Fortress of Meropide?

140151104.text: Hahaha, that's right! I've finally finished serving my time. Gotta say, turns out I was a lot tougher than I thought!

140151105.text: After I got out, I immediately made a beeline back to Poisson. You could say that familiar briny smell became a primal call, urging me to forget everything else and just come back home.

140151106.text: You wouldn't believe how much I've missed Melissa's Grilled Fish — I dreamed about it every time I had to get a Welfare Meal down there underneath the sea!

140151107.text: It's good to have you back, Colter. You look as well as ever.

140151109.text: Ah, let me introduce you. This is Colter, another of Spina di Rosula's members. He was found guilty and sentenced to the Fortress of Meropide some time ago.

140151110.text: But looking at it now, it was probably another one of Marcel's plots while he worked at the Confrerie of Cabriere.

140151111.text: Wait, wait, Mr. Marcel? What do you mean, he was involved in some sort of plot?

140151112.text: Have you not heard anything at all about the "Water from the Primordial Sea" case?

140151113.text: Well, I know that Fontaine got flooded, but then the water levels miraculously receded. I thought that was all there was to it, and didn't care to ask for any more details. Do you mean... Mr. Marcel was somehow involved with all of that?

140151114.text: Looks like we'll have to explain everything from the top. That case... A lot of things have happened in Poisson since then.

140151115.text: First things first, let me introduce you to these two. They're my most trusted partners, and they've been with me through thick and thin. Now, you could call them Spina di Rosula's VIP helpers.

140151116.text: Oh, nice to meet you! I don't recall Navia ever generously complimenting anyone like that before, so you must be pretty amazing to get that from her!

140151117.text: Hehe, yeah, we are indeed pretty amazing, but we've been cool since before we even met her!

140151119.text: Humble again as always, I see, even when I was totally sincere with my praise.

140151122.text: Nice, nice. Spina di Rosula always seems to attract great people.

140151123.text: Oh, that reminds me — where are Melus and Silver? Aren't they always by your side?

140151125.text: Colter, a lot of things happened while you were gone. As you can see, even Poisson isn't quite the same as... how it was before you left.

140151126.text: They lost their lives keeping me safe during the flood.

140151128.text: This isn't some kind of morbid welcome-home prank, right? You're just scaring me on purpose, because I don't know anything about what's happened...

140151129.text: I'm sorry, but it's the truth. They weren't the only people we lost, either. Many others, including Melissa, also lost their lives in the disaster.

140151130.text: Melus, and Melissa... Dead? They're just... gone?

140151131.text: Melus... I was planning to give him a surprise gift once I ran into him again in town. Ah, I can't believe it...

140151133.text: Melus and Colter were friends for many years, and even served on many missions together during the early days of the Spina. I can understand how he feels.

140151134.text: Let's sit down somewhere, so I can tell you everything that has happened while you were gone. Fair warning, there was... a lot.

140151121.text: Wait, now you suddenly resist taking a dig at Paimon?

140150501.text: Navia explains everything that has happened recently to Colter.

140150502.text: All of this... It's unbelievable... I can't believe that those stories were real, it all really happened. Has the world gone mad?

140150505.text: I think you and I both feel the same way about the profound tragedy of Melus's loss, and... the sheer depravity of Marcel's actions.

140150506.text: I thought Mr. Marcel would always stand by the Spina... Everything he had, the Spina gave to him.

140150507.text: It's unconscionable to have received all that, and yet still plot to kidnap and dissolve you for his insane research.

140150508.text: The good news is that the Confrerie of Cabriere is no more. Gone with them, too, is the entire Sinthe manufacturing and distribution network.

140150509.text: We've finally closed the curtain on that long struggle.

140150510.text: Are you sure? But if Marcel wanted to rebel against us, he probably sent word in secret to Romeuf.

140150512.text: Not a name I've heard before, either.

140150513.text: Florent should remember him. You see, there was once a major internal dispute regarding funding the construction of the aquabus lines.

140150514.text: Romeuf was the leader of the faction that thought such a vast sum of Mora would be better spent improving the town of Poisson.

140150515.text: But Mr. Callas believed that an opportunity to collaborate with the Court of Fontaine and the Fontaine Research Institute was hard to come by, and would allow us to build many valuable relationships.

140150516.text: Not only would the aquabus be a good business investment, it would also boost our reputation among the general populace, eventually paying us massive dividends down the line.

140150517.text: But the two couldn't come to an agreement. Romeuf ended up taking a lot of people with him when he left Spina di Rosula altogether, and the split was on extremely bad terms.

140150518.text: Ugh, and with Papa's stubbornness, I can definitely imagine how it must have gone down...

140150519.text: And, of course, when he was suffering the slings and arrows of outrageous injustice... Those "relationships" that he spent a fortune to build didn't help in the least.

140150520.text: Yeah... You could say it was the price he paid for sticking to his beliefs.

140150521.text: That couldn't have been the first time a dispute like that happened, right?

140150522.text: Oh, that's a good point! If Callas was really as stubborn as you say, then wouldn't he have argued with the rank and file all the time?

140150523.text: Oh yeah, it eventually became a thing that just happened on every day that ended with "y." But, Navia... I mean, Boss, you might not know this, but he wasn't always like that.

140150524.text: He used to be a lot better with taking counsel. With him listening to our advice, and Ms. Clementine also frequently on our side, it was pretty smooth sailing for a good many years.

140150525.text: But on the matter of the aquabus, even Ms. Clementine completely stood by Mr. Callas' side.

140150526.text: Huh, I never knew... But from my perspective, Romeuf's position had a lot going for it. Couldn't they have sat down and talked it out?

140150527.text: I think the aquabus was just the straw that broke the camel's back. On that topic, they eventually came to a rather... radical conclusion.

140150528.text: They believed that... Ms. Clementine lost her ability to serve as an impartial mediator when she became pregnant with Callas' child.

140150529.text: So... they thought she had betrayed them?

140150530.text: But that doesn't make any sense. Before she was their mediator, my mother was also her own person and a member of the Spina. She should have the right to take any side she wished.

140150531.text: Yeah, but to them, even taking a side was betrayal enough. They felt like their voices could no longer be heard once their sole mediator had gone over to the other side.

140150532.text: Of course, Ms. Clementine then passed away, and Mr. Callas began to regard the completion of the aquabus project as her final wish. With that, the last hope of reconciliation was gone.

140150534.text: From that point on, Romeuf and his people cut ties with the Spina, and never gave us any kind of professional or personal courtesy ever again.

140150535.text: Perhaps they've regarded us as enemies ever since they left. But even so, there is still no proof that they ever acted in concert with Marcel.

140150536.text: I've also heard that they aren't in a good financial position, so they've been lying low for a while. But as long as they exist, they'll continue to be a threat.

140150537.text: I think Colter's got a point. Both Marcel and Romeuf had my father in their sights for a very long time.

140150538.text: Even though Marcel's faction has been dissolved, we still don't know anything about Romeuf's whereabouts. If they're still trying to get revenge on us...

140150539.text: ...With how distracted and vulnerable we are, now would be the best time.

140150540.text: Good thinking, Boss. We should keep an eye on them at all times. I'll let my men know right away.

140150541.text: Mhm, thank you for that, Florent. And Colter, thank you for telling me about this as well.

140150542.text: Don't worry, it's nothing. Do you have a moment right now? How about we go out for a walk?

140150543.text: I've heard so many incredulous things today... I'm finding it a bit hard to calm down, even now. I mean, to think that I'll just... never see them again...

140150544.text: In that case, why don't we go back to the Court? I can pick up Adele's uniform while we're there as well. It'll save Florent's guys a trip.

140150545.text: Want to come with me again, you two? You don't mind, do you, Colter?

140150546.text: O—Oh, of course, that's fine by me.

140150547.text: Then let's go! Paimon feels like a lot's hinging on this visit.

subQuests.subQuestName: Relax with Colter as you head to the Court of Fontaine
Relax with Colter as you head to the Court of Fontaine

140150601.text: Well, we've walked far enough for now. Let's take a break!

140150602.text: Since we're out for a walk, we shouldn't stress too much about the destination.

140150603.text: Hehe, I've grown old, so I'm not as fit as before. It's a good thing that at least my work down in the Fortress was quite the workout.

140150604.text: Well, Paimon thinks you're doing great! We didn't have to slow down for you at all.

140150605.text: Back in the days before the aquabus lines were built, we often had to hike north with our goods, then catch a boat to the Court.

140150606.text: Melus and I must have traveled this way hundreds of times. When we were tired, we would lay down for a while on the grass, and when we were hungry, we'd catch a fish or two.

140150607.text: The Spina was still on the rise back then. Mr. Callas was generous, and everyone had the chance to strike it rich. So of course, we all worked really hard.

140150608.text: And now, in the blink of an eye, the aquabus lines have been built, and this road has fallen into disuse.

140150609.text: I don't really think that's a bad thing, though.

140150610.text: Oh, I know. I was just being a little nostalgic.

140150611.text: Then let's stay here a bit longer. Anyone want snacks?

140150612.text: Oh! Is this another chance to try some of Navia's macarons? Paimon's been dreaming of them!

140150613.text: Hahaha, yep! I figured you wouldn't say no to a few more.

140150614.text: Oh, wait, let me check if I have all the ingredients... *sigh* Melus and Silver used to take care of tasks like this.

140150615.text: Okay, the stove's looking good, and as for the ingredients...

140150616.text: ...Seems like we're all out of flour and sugar. The two most important ingredients of all.

140150618.text: Oh, would you? But it would be too much to ask you to go on a trip just for those...

140150619.text: #We should contribute to making the macarons, too! Don't worry, we cook out in the wild all the time, so {M#he}{F#she} should have some stuff on hand.

140150620.text: Oh, that's great! Then I'll leave the ingredient gathering to you. As long as we have some sweet flowers and wheat, I can start the baking.

140150621.text: Then I'll go look for some boxes nearby, for a makeshift table and chairs.

140150622.text: Great, then I'll prep the stove. Let's get to work, everyone!

subQuests.subQuestName: Give the Wheat and Sweet Flower to Navia

140150701.text: How did it go? Did you find the ingredients?

140150801.text: You've all done your part! Just leave the rest to me.

140150802.text: Navia bakes a batch of macarons with her usual gusto.

140150803.text: Whoa, these macarons look and taste macanificent! Your cooking is as good as ever, Navia!

140150804.text: Boss's baking skills have always been famous. Everyone in the Spina knows how exceptionally talented she is.

140150805.text: Hehe, it's just a hobby. There's no need to praise me for it like that.

140150806.text: Have you two seriously never considered joining us? You're so close to the Boss, and she obviously trusts you with all her heart, so...

140150808.text: I see... Is that why you have to always stay on the road?

140150811.text: Haha, you just happened to walk in on our little reunion. It's actually been quite a while since we last spent time together.

140150812.text: Adventurers never stay in one place for long. The name of Spina di Rosula would just tie them down.

140150813.text: Besides, after everything we've been through together, I'm sure our hearts would remain intertwined even if we found ourselves on opposite sides of the world!

140150810.text: Hahaha, was it that obvious? I just thought you would be a great fit, that's all.

140150101.text: Well, if it isn't my dear partners!

140150103.text: Hehe, I didn't expect to run into you guys here today. Are you headed somewhere?

140150106.text: How about you, Navia? Are you still busy rebuilding Poisson?

140150107.text: Yeah, there are still tons of issues to fix. It certainly hasn't been easy.

140150401.text: #Boss, you're back! {NICKNAME} and Paimon, welcome back to Poisson.

140150402.text: Oh hey! Fancy seeing you again, Florent! Is it your turn to take care of Navia now?

140150403.text: Hey, I can totally take care of myself! For the time being, I'll go around without any attendants.

140150404.text: We did hand over some of Melus' old responsibilities to Florent, though. It's been really nice to have him around to help out.

140150405.text: Thank you for the compliment, Boss.

140150406.text: As you see, I've been working closely with the Boss on rebuilding Poisson.

140150407.text: Mr. Melus was an extremely capable and respected member of the Spina. I've got some really big shoes to fill.

140150408.text: Alright, alright, there's no need to be so formal. Everyone's practically old friends by now.

140150409.text: Were you waiting here for me? Did we manage to make any progress on the statue?

140150410.text: Yeah, we contacted a sculptor about the job, but they can't get started on sourcing a correctly sized block without knowing the design that we want to use first.

140150412.text: Ah, so basically, we've been meaning to commission a statue of my parents in commemoration of everything they've done for the Spina and the town of Poisson.

140150413.text: But since my father was known as "Callas the Unfaithful" for the longest time, it would have been too controversial to commission a statue of him.

140150414.text: But now that his name has been cleared, and the town is also being rebuilt, I thought this would be the perfect chance to actually realize this dream.

140150415.text: The funds to build the statue were freely donated by the people of Poisson, to show their appreciation for Ms. Clementine and Mr. Callas and everything they did.

140150416.text: Shouldn't Navia be featured with them, too?

140150417.text: Me? I'm just the newbie President that's running around and causing everyone trouble.

140150418.text: Maybe we can have this conversation again in a few decades, once I've done more for the town and the people.

140150419.text: Hey, there's no need to be so humble! Didn't you just help save the entire country?

140150420.text: I agree wholeheartedly. I also believe that Boss should have a place on the statue.

140150421.text: Hey, if you keep inflating my ego like this, I might just float off into the sky with my parasol.

140150422.text: Haha, just kidding! There's no way that I'd accept that kind of compliment at face value. At a minimum, I'd have to match what my father did for the people.

140150425.text: Haha, thanks for the vote of confidence! I just don't think I'm ready yet.

140150426.text: Anyway, Florent, now it's up to us to confirm the final design, right?

140150427.text: Mhm. We can ask the sculptor to start looking for a good block once we've decided on the poses for Ms. Clementine and Mr. Callas.

140150428.text: But we haven't had any real discussions yet on the possible designs. I feel like I should get a few promising designs first, and then send them over to you to review...

140150429.text: Eh, there's no need for all that. Let's decide on a design right now!

140150901.text: Well, if it isn't my dear partners!

140150903.text: Hehe, I didn't expect to run into you guys here today. Are you headed somewhere?

140150906.text: How about you, Navia? Are you still busy rebuilding Poisson?

140150907.text: Heh, we've wrapped up most of the rebuilding, but there are still a few things left to take care of.

140159901.text: Are we not taking the boat this time?

140159902.text: It's nice to walk from time to time, isn't it? Think of it as something like a hiking trip.

140159903.text: Once we're there, we can stay a few days before we return.

140159904.text: Sounds good... I haven't walked this road in a long time.
